figures.title: Efficient frontier
figures.note: Expected returns are historical means, used here only to give the frontier a vertical axis — see the caveat below.

notes: Minimum variance needs no expected returns, which is exactly what makes it robust: μ is the noisiest input in mean-variance and the one that drives error maximisation. The long-only constraint acts as an implicit regulariser (Jagannathan & Ma 2003).
The frontier does need μ, and here it is the historical mean — a poor forecast, shown for construction purposes only. In practice μ would come from Black-Litterman or explicit views.

Risk parity holds every asset by construction and minimum variance will drop assets outright, so the two differ most where the covariance is least trustworthy. HRP never inverts Σ at all, which is why it degrades gracefully when the estimate is poorly conditioned — see METHODOLOGY §12.
The long-short solution reaches 10.11% volatility but with 1.45× gross exposure: large offsetting legs fitted to the noise in Σ.
